    BO13a Lemma 5 a) #

    Let σ s be long in a chain Z, let (α v', β w') be a contour of σ s, and suppose every long morphism occurs in a contour. If ρ (s+1) factors through neither first arrow α, β, we get a contradiction (MulBasis.lemma5a).

    Following BO13a, we walk along the chain to the next long morphism τ (Nat.find). If τ = ρ (s+1), four first arrows leave x (s+1). Otherwise τ is some ρ (s+1+L+1) (case A) or σ (s+1+L) (case B). If some long morphism does not divide τ, we quotient by it (lemma5a_caseA, lemma5a_caseB); otherwise τ is the only long morphism up to the factorization order and the top states lemma5a_top, lemma5a_topB apply.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.RayQuiver.MulBasis.lemma5a {P : Type} [CategoryTheory.Category.{0, 0} P] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroMorphisms P] [IsRayCategory P] [Fintype P] [DecidableEq P] [IsFiniteRayCategory P] {k : Type u} [Field k] [Infinite k] {A : Type u} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] (B : MulBasis k P A) (hmin : ∀ (I : TwoSidedIdeal A), I ≠ ⊥ → Statement.IsRepresentationFinite (A ⧸ TwoSidedIdeal.asIdeal I)) (hL : RayCat.LeftCancel P) (hR : RayCat.RightCancel P) (hQ : OneSidedCyclic P) (hcont : ∀ {a b : P} (μ : a ⟶ b), RayCat.IsLong μ → ¬RayCat.NotInContour μ) (Z : RayCat.ZChain P) (s : ℕ) (hσ : RayCat.IsLong (Z.σ s)) (hnext : ∃ (j : ℕ), RayCat.IsLong (Z.σ (s + 1 + j))) {a₁ b₁ : RayCat.RayVert P} (α : RayCat.RayVert.mk (Z.x (s + 1)) ⟶ a₁) (β : RayCat.RayVert.mk (Z.x (s + 1)) ⟶ b₁) (v' : Quiver.Path a₁ (RayCat.RayVert.mk (Z.z s))) (w' : Quiver.Path b₁ (RayCat.RayVert.mk (Z.z s))) (hv : RayCat.pathVal (α.toPath.comp v') = Z.σ s) (hw : RayCat.pathVal (β.toPath.comp w') = Z.σ s) (hni : ¬RayCat.Interlaced (α.toPath.comp v') (β.toPath.comp w')) (hα : ¬∃ (g : a₁.out ⟶ Z.z (s + 1)), CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (↑α) g = Z.ρ (s + 1)) (hβ : ¬∃ (g : b₁.out ⟶ Z.z (s + 1)), CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (↑β) g = Z.ρ (s + 1)) :
    False

    BO13a Lemma 5 a). If every long morphism occurs in a contour, σ s is long with contour (α v', β w'), and a long morphism follows in the chain, then ρ (s+1) factors through α or β.
